title: AI-Driven SDLC Framework v2.0 Master
subtitle: Spec-as-Code Ecosystem, Ruflo Swarm Orchestration, WSCI Context Engineering & Jidoka
summary: AI-driven software engineering ecosystem integrating the Spec-as-Code paradigm (META SPEC), swarm topology (Ruflo), WSCI context engineering, and Jidoka quality gates (Andon Cord).
overview: The Framework v2.0 Master is a software engineering ecosystem that transforms stochastic AI models into structured operational team members. It abandons raw source code as the single source of truth in favor of the Spec-as-Code paradigm via META SPEC (Project Constitution). The architecture orchestrates a specialist agent swarm (Ruflo) led by a central Chief of Staff orchestrator, leveraging WSCI context engineering (Write, Select, Compress, Isolate), Git Worktree isolation, and continuous Jidoka quality control (Andon Cord).
roleDescription: AI Solutions Architect, Tech Lead & Engineering Process Architect.
responsibilities: Conceived and designed the hierarchical swarm topology (Ruflo) with central Chief of Staff orchestration and isolated working memory.
Structured technical governance guidelines and Jidoka quality gates (Andon Cord) for immediate clean resets upon anomaly detection.
Engineered the WSCI context methodology (Write, Select, Compress, Isolate) to eliminate AI context window degradation and distraction.
Created the SPARC+DD lifecycle and integrated the Spec-as-Code paradigm via META SPEC (Project Constitution).

challengesAndSolutions.challenge: Context window degradation (poisoning and distraction) when AI agents operate across large repositories or long execution runs.
challengesAndSolutions.solution: Implemented WSCI Context Engineering (Write, Select, Compress, Isolate) paired with AST selection tools and specialist agent isolation via Git Worktrees (Superpowers).

futureEvolution: Decentralized telemetry implementation for measuring sub-agent efficiency (time/tokens) under Zero-Trust policies.
Automated Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) generation from synchronous multi-agent debates during the SPARC+DD Architecture phase.
